body.cap: An example of an AI tracking and beamforming-based wireless power transmission system delivering RF energy to multiple devices | Provided by Warp Solution

body.x: Warp Solution Inc. (CEO Kyunghak Lee) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from Tuesday, January 6 to Friday, January 9 (local time).

Warp Solution is a Korean fabless company that has commercialized long-range, multi-device simultaneous wireless power transmission (WTP) technology using radio-frequency (RF) technology. The company has developed core semiconductor products for 5G- and RF-based wireless charging technologies, including ultra-compact RF power amplifiers and high-frequency rectifier components. It has secured several domestic and international intellectual property rights.

Building on this foundation, Warp Solution is also developing a radio energy platform with strong scalability across advanced industries such as IoT, smart homes, industrial automation, and healthcare, as well as AI-powered power control solutions. Through these efforts, the company aims to universalize innovative wireless charging environments across industrial and smart device markets.

At CES 2026, Warp Solution will present its WTP system that combines AI tracking and beamforming technologies. The system uses vision AI camera algorithms to track the location of receivers in real time within the coverage area, optimizes the path and angle of long-range RF energy delivery through AI beamforming, and implements adaptive RF directivity tailored in real time to constantly changing charging locations and environments.

The RF energy transmitted over long distances is converted into usable charging power through dedicated receivers. Warp Solution integrates its core semiconductor technologies, including RF power amplifier devices and high-frequency rectifier components, to deliver more stable, advanced energy. In particular, the company’s proprietary RF-DC rectifier chip “WEP” series supports power conversion efficiency of up to 60 percent.

In addition, efficient power distribution and transmission algorithms enable simultaneous wireless charging of multiple devices, while support for a wide frequency range from 100 MHz to 6 GHz ensures broad charging compatibility. These technological strengths translate into significantly greater freedom and spatial flexibility compared to conventional wireless charging methods.

Warp Solution plans to introduce its differentiated wireless charging technology at CES 2026 and accelerate full-scale expansion into global industries. A company official said, “Our multi-device long-range wireless charging platform delivers high utility across fields such as IoT, smart homes, and smart factories,” adding, “For example, when applied to industrial IoT sensors or edge devices that operate in large spaces with frequent movement or where battery replacement is difficult, it can serve as core infrastructure that maximizes productivity and operational continuity.”

The official continued, “By enabling stable and efficient power transmission anytime and anywhere, we aim to attract partners and potential customers across a wide range of domestic and global industries, while promoting the spread and standardization of next-generation wireless charging platforms,” emphasizing that “this year’s CES will be a critical testing ground for determining the success of these goals.”
